ideas.title: Shopping a bronze or catastrophic ACA plan this open enrollment? Under the 2025 budget law it now comes with HSA eligibility. Here's what that does and doesn't save you
ideas.angle: With benchmark premiums up and more people choosing cheaper, high-deductible plans, KFF explains the budget law's change that makes more Marketplace plans HSA-eligible. The roundup item covers who can now open an HSA, the tax break it gives, and the catch: it only helps people with spare cash to put in, while the deductible stays the same.
ideas.why_now: ACA open enrollment opened Nov 1 and runs to Jan 15. People choosing between metal tiers now need to know which plans pair with an HSA. KFF published the brief Nov 2.
ideas.is_it_real: Independent KFF analysis of a change in federal law. The digest summary only says the reconciliation law 'expanded access to HSA-eligible plans and accounts' on the Marketplaces. It has no figures. The details (which tiers qualify, the effective date, any direct-primary-care provision, contribution limits) have to come from the KFF brief itself before the item runs. No numbers are stated here.
ideas.primary_test: The KFF brief and the HSA provisions of the 2025 reconciliation law (Public Law 119-21), checked against IRS guidance on HSA eligibility for bronze and catastrophic plans
ideas.other_peg: ACA open enrollment, Nov 1 to Jan 15

items.title: Explaining Health Savings Accounts in the Affordable Care Act Marketplaces
items.summary: This brief examines how the budget reconciliation law expanded access to HSA-eligible plans and accounts on the ACA Marketplaces and what these changes means for enrollees
